items.stem: Why is it important to scope an AI project to something small and achievable?

options.text: A focused goal can be completed, tested and evaluated honestly within the time and data available
options.rationale: Correct: realistic scope makes a project finishable and assessable.

options.text: Small projects are the only ones that use computers
options.rationale: Projects of any size use computers; scope is about feasibility.

options.text: A vague, huge goal is always more impressive
options.rationale: Unrealistic scope usually leads to unfinished, untested work.

options.text: Scoping has no effect on the outcome
options.rationale: Scope strongly affects whether the project succeeds.

items.explanation: Correct: realistic scope makes a project finishable and assessable.

items.stem: Which TWO practices make an AI project honest and responsible? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Evaluating it on new data, not just the data used to build it
options.rationale: Correct: testing on new examples gives an honest result.
Correct: being honest about limits is responsible.

options.text: Only showing the one example where it worked
Using people's private data without their consent
options.rationale: Using private data without consent is unethical.

items.explanation: Correct: testing on new examples gives an honest result.

items.stem: Your project worked perfectly in one demo. What is the most honest next step before claiming success?

options.text: Test it on several new, unseen examples and report how it really performs
options.rationale: Correct: a single successful demo is not proof of reliability.
One demo does not prove reliability.

options.text: Hide any examples where it fails

options.rationale: Further testing on new data is exactly what is needed.
